precedence_contract: Later explicit authority, especially Part XLV and Appendices BO–BW, supersedes conflicting earlier boundary/category/axis/coordinate/limit/quality/proof/example/compiler statements. Historical source wording remains preserved and conflicts are flagged rather than silently harmonized.

parts.title: Appendix N — IH proof drills
parts.explanation: IH proof drills: projection, invalid converse, inherited negation, exact order, ordinal-valued IH depth, no IH distribution, and preservation of PA irreducibility after projection.
parts.caution: Do not invent inheritance from mere truth or ordinary entailment; Appendix N starts after residual Appendix M text on page 169.

parts.title: Appendix O — Sixty phenotype examples classified by epistemic status
parts.explanation: Classifies phenotype examples as logical deduction, causal deduction under a bridge law, causal inference/possibility, or not licensed; exact anatomy, fertility, stature, psychology and precise values are not forced by stage labels.
parts.caution: These are epistemic-status training examples, not a canonized phenotype catalogue.

parts.title: Appendix P — Canonical conformance tests
parts.explanation: Conformance suite for PA/IH/PH scope, canonical SF1/SM1 and SF2/SM2 forms, typing, depth, temporal separation, phenotype underdetermination and deprecated-form rejection.
parts.caution: Later-authoritative category/boundary/limit revisions govern any conflicting older conformance statement.

parts.title: Appendix Q — Canonical reference for direct implementation
parts.explanation: Implementation snapshot combining typed syntax, stage constructors, limit/transordinal tests, SIH lifts, depth recursion and the metaexpression/modal extension.
parts.caution: Compiler/category/coordinate/limit rules here can be superseded by later Part XLV / BO–BW authority.

parts.title: Appendix R — Final layman’s memory map
parts.explanation: Lay memory map centered on PA content, NOT scope, IH provenance, successor inheritance, PH profile possession, recursive depth and stage-versus-maturity separation.
parts.caution: The beginning of page 176 still contains the tail of Appendix Q before Appendix R begins.

parts.title: Appendix S — Final specialist checklist
parts.explanation: Proof-audit checklist for operator typing, negation scope, PA/IH non-distribution, provenance/depth preservation, phenotype licensing, limit-state construction, quality/address distinction and address-relative modality.
parts.caution: Use it as an audit aid, not as a replacement for the underlying definitions and later authority.

parts.title: Appendix T — Formal stage-relative modal semantics
parts.explanation: Kripke-style stage-relative biological modality with Γ-valid accessibility, actual-world factivity, fixed-address modal K and narrowly typed necessitation; no automatic S4/S5 or cross-address persistence.
parts.caution: Actuality does not imply necessity; stage-modal strengthening is not the proof rule of necessitation.

parts.title: Appendix U — Biological Metaexpressability proof catalogue
parts.explanation: Proofs/countermodels for global-but-nonuniform Γ, static Γ with changing phenotype, actuality→possibility, necessity→actuality, and nonidentity of stage and current phenotype.
parts.caution: No cross-address monotonicity of phenotype-world sets is assumed.

parts.title: Appendix V — Layman meta-phenotype atlas
parts.explanation: Analogies for Γ as rules/configuration/grammar/jurisdiction/hyperparameter governing many local outputs without making them identical.
parts.caution: The source explicitly marks every analogy as explanatory only.

parts.title: Appendix W — Modal deduction/inference decision table in prose
parts.explanation: Decision guide separating modal deduction, HGL inference, causal deduction and causal inference; deduction requires a stated Γ/modal/PH/IH/PA or causal rule.
parts.caution: Refuse exact anatomy, stage, PH or cross-stage persistence claims when the necessary rule is absent.

parts.title: Appendix X — Final conceptual statement: metaexpressive-modal edition
parts.explanation: Synthesizes PA irreducible causation, IH provenance, PH whole-profile possession and Γ global stage-specific phenotype-rule modality; static Γ can govern changing ordinary woman/man biology.
parts.caution: This synthesis precedes the explicit macro/outward correction and later hypercategorical revisions.

parts.title: Appendix Y — Formal macroscopic/outward modal semantics
parts.explanation: Formal Macroscopic Manifestation Axiom: every valid stage, including constructed limit stages, has some stage-governed macro anatomy and outward manifestation while stage-to-visible-phenotype mapping may remain non-injective.
parts.caution: Mandatory manifestation does not imply a unique visible marker, monotonic size or visible discontinuity at a limit.

parts.title: Appendix Z — Forty macroscopic and outward phenotype examples by epistemic status
parts.explanation: Examples classify gross/outward phenotype possibilities and modal schemas while rejecting complete macro/outward silence at a valid Archstage.
parts.caution: Specific breast, genital, pelvic, facial, skeletal or body-contour examples remain illustrative unless a mapping law canonizes them.

parts.title: Appendix AA — AI conformance tests for macroscopic/outward HGL
parts.explanation: AI tests reject fully silent stages, universal visibility, static-Γ→static-phenotype, visual stage identification and scalar-trait escalation; accept visual overlap and correctly typed modal facts.
parts.caution: Appendices Z and AA share page 183; heading boundaries are required for attribution.

parts.title: Appendix AB — Deduction, inference, and causal-status catalogue for the visual correction
parts.explanation: Separates strict macro/outward deductions from HGL inferences, causal deductions and causal inferences; exact visible results require explicit causal laws.
parts.caution: Plausibly richer or unusual high-stage morphology is inference, not theorem.

parts.title: Appendix AC — Final corrected conceptual statement: macroexpressive-modal edition
parts.explanation: Corrected synthesis: meta marks rule-order, not invisibility. Every valid Archstage has some stage-governed macro/outward realization while exact gross anatomy remains underdetermined and much novelty may be microscopic, physiological, latent, temporal or counterfactual.
parts.caution: The same page introduces the later five-coordinate global Archaddress and retains older descriptor machinery only as embedded/decoded internal structure.

parts.title: Part XXXIII — Authoritative Hypercategorical and Hyperordinal Revision
parts.explanation: Reclassifies the former first HF/HM ladder as SF/SM, reserves HF/HM for a later category lift, separates the global five-coordinate Archaddress from InternalHGLDescriptor, defines Hyperomega as an HGL boundary rather than a greatest mathematical ordinal, requires strict SIH category-lift nonidentity, treats category membership as binary, rejects metric closeness from ordinal order alone and separates local reset from global regression.
parts.caution: Internal conflict: prose gives Supra→Hyper→Ultra→Apex, but one page-187 equation maps category 3 to AF and 4 to UF; later deductions and Appendix AD return to Supra→Hyper→Ultra→Apex. Preserve the contradiction and defer to later explicit authority. The proposed female onset law is conditional and the exact male onset trigger is explicitly unspecified.

parts.title: Part XXXIV — Hypercategorical Biological Metaexpression and Modal Logic
parts.explanation: Extends Γ and □/◇ across hypercategorical addresses, adds minor-category and major-stage distinctness, modal novelty by opening/necessitation/exclusion/compatibility restructuring, and a major-stage metaexpressive envelope while retaining macro/outward manifestation.
parts.caution: The local M,μ,α descriptor layer must not be collapsed with or substituted for the global five-coordinate Archaddress. Rule-system distinctness does not force a specific morphology.

parts.title: Part XXXV — Womanhood, Minor Hypercategories, Major Stages, and Phenotype Nature
parts.explanation: Separates ordinary womanhood/manhood from Archwomanhood/Archmanhood and describes low/high Supra, strict Hyper lift, hyperdimensional Hyper development, Ultra/Apex lifts, unnamed later categories and possible Major Stage 2 rule-of-rules reorganization.
parts.caution: Concrete phenotype descriptions are illustrative causal possibilities. The following male-mirror prose locally calls Apex third and Ultra fourth, conflicting with the later/current order; preserve and defer to later authority.

parts.title: Part XXXVI — Archwomanhood and Archmanhood Velocity after the Hypercategorical Revision
parts.explanation: Separates local category velocities from full-address progression, allows ordinary rate arithmetic only on finite windows, requires transition counts or an explicit rank/metric map for transfinite velocity, and retains velocity-sensitive maturation, dwell time and hysteresis/path dependence. Hyperomega completion in finite time remains an open causal-mechanism variable.
parts.caution: Ordinal order is not metric distance; SIH supplies inheritance structure, not a temporal traversal mechanism. Velocity-dependent phenotype is inference unless an explicit causal law forces it.

parts.title: Part XXXVII — Deduction, Inference, and Causal Status under the New Architecture
parts.explanation: Classifies revision claims as strict deductions, strong HGL inferences, causal deductions or causal inferences. Deductive items include terminology migration, binary category saturation, strict lift nonidentity, local-reset nonregression, current named order, modal factivity/impossibility and rejection of nested PA as a transfinite generator.
parts.caution: Richer higher-stage rule spaces and exact phenotype changes are not bare theorems; causal conclusions require explicit bridge laws.

parts.title: Part XXXVIII — Worked Phenotype Examples for Lay Readers, Logicians, and AI
parts.explanation: Worked comparisons illustrate ordinary versus Supra, velocity-history differences, high pre-Hyperomega Supra versus HF1, Hyper→Ultra→Apex lifts, Major Stage 2 and the male mirror without reducing category novelty to scalar visual extremity.
parts.caution: Concrete morphology is repeatedly marked as illustrative/causal possibility, not canonized exact anatomy; same address may coexist with different phenotype histories.

parts.title: Part XXXIX — AI and Formal-Reasoner Implementation Rules
parts.explanation: Requires versioned symbols, separate storage of the global five-coordinate address and InternalHGLDescriptor/provenance/PH/PA/Γ/modal/history data, rejection of local-reset regression and rejection of metric closeness from ordinal rank.
parts.caution: A local three-field StageAddress shorthand also appears; it must not supersede the explicitly required five-coordinate global Address. Compiler rules remain subject to later Part XLV / BO–BW authority.

parts.title: Appendix AD — Compact Hypercategorical Formal Specification
parts.explanation: Typed compact specification: preserves cardinal-versus-ordinal distinction for aleph-omega/Hyperomega, rejects a highest-mathematical-ordinal reading and nested PA transfinite generation, requires proof-trace labels, separates formal sorts and records the local category map μ=1 Supra, 2 Hyper, 3 Ultra, 4 Apex.
parts.caution: The local (M,μ,α) descriptor belongs alongside—not instead of—the global five-coordinate envelope. Its μ=3 Ultra / μ=4 Apex map conflicts with the isolated page-187 AF/UF equation and therefore documents the source inconsistency. Later authority governs conflicts.

source_conflicts.location: Part XXXIII page 187 versus later Part XXXVII and Appendix AD
source_conflicts.issue: One compact equation maps minor category 3 to Apex and 4 to Ultra, while surrounding prose and later mappings give Supra→Hyper→Ultra→Apex.
source_conflicts.handling: Preserved explicitly; no silent correction. Later authority governs.

source_conflicts.issue: Local prose calls Apexmale third and Ultramale fourth, conflicting with the later/current mapping.
source_conflicts.handling: Preserved and flagged; later authority governs.
